description: Voice Watchers is a solo-developer team from the Dominican Republic for NASA Space Apps 2026 "Abandoned but not Forgotten". Built "Echoes of the Void": an interactive web console where students ages 10-16 wake up historic NASA hardware (Apollo 11, InSight, Voyager 1) via first-person radio transmissions and hands-on science mini-labs. Stack: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, Canvas. Bilingual (EN/ES) with built-in Classroom Mode. Created independently by a 15-year-old student passionate about space STEM.
summary: Echoes of the Void is an interactive, bilingual (EN/ES) space archaeology web console designed for students ages 10 to 16 for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge ("Abandoned but not Forgotten"). Built independently using lightweight web technologies (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, and HTML5 Canvas) so any school computer can run it without installation, the platform allows users to tune into real NASA coordinates across the Moon, Mars, and deep space to wake up historic, dormant hardware, specifically the Apollo 11 Lunar Laser Ranging Retroreflector, the Mars InSight lander, and the Voyager 1 interstellar probe. Instead of leaving these iconic missions buried in complex technical repositories like LROC, HiRISE, and JPL Horizons, Echoes of the Void transforms raw archival telemetry into immersive first-person radio transmissions paired with hands-on science mini-labs. Students actively fire simulated lunar laser beams to verify orbital drift, analyze Marsquake seismic P-waves and S-waves to map planetary layers, and decode interstellar cosmic ray telemetry. This project is important because it bridges the gap between cold scientific data and accessible STEM education, featuring an instant English-Spanish toggle and a built-in Classroom Mode with comprehension quizzes and printable worksheets to ensure humanity's silent space pioneers continue inspiring future explorers worldwide.
details:
Echoes of the Void functions as a browser-based deep-space archaeology heads-up display (HUD) designed for students ages 10 to 16. Users select from three historic targets, the Apollo 11 Lunar Laser Ranging Retroreflector, the Mars InSight Lander (alongside Opportunity), and the Voyager 1 interstellar probe, tuning into their exact NASA mission coordinates. Once connected, the console displays real-time archival telemetry and streams a first-person "radio transmission" written from the hardware's perspective using a live typewriter effect. Each mission features a custom interactive science mini-lab where students fire simulated lunar lasers (299,792 km/s) to measure the Moon's orbital drift, analyze Marsquake S1222a seismic P-waves and S-waves, and decode interstellar cosmic ray telemetry at the heliopause.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

  • Core Stack: Pure HTML5, CSS3, and Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+) for maximum speed, zero external dependencies, and instant offline/online portability.
  • Interactive Simulations: Custom HTML5 Canvas rendering pipelines to animate starfields, laser trajectories, seismic waveforms, and binary telemetry streams.
  • Data Sources: Authentic mission coordinates, timelines, and scientific parameters sourced from NASA LROC, HiRISE, SEIS (InSight), and JPL Horizons archives.
  • Development & Deployment: Developed and tested on a standard Windows 11 laptop and deployed publicly via CodePen for instant cross-device browser access.

Creativity & Design Factors Considered

  • First-Person "Space Archaeology" Narrative: Instead of presenting static encyclopedic articles, the project gives silent hardware a human voice, turning cold engineering logs into emotional, memorable stories of exploration and endurance.
  • Accessibility & Low-Spec Hardware Compatibility: Recognizing that many schools rely on basic computers or restricted operating systems, the app was engineered to require zero downloads, zero plugins, and minimal bandwidth.
  • Linguistic Inclusion & Classroom Integration: To remove language barriers across Latin America and the Caribbean, the console features a one-click English / Spanish toggle that dynamically translates the entire interface, transmissions, and labs. It also includes a dedicated Classroom Mode with an interactive comprehension quiz and a one-click printable worksheet generator for teachers.

Benefits & Intended Impact

Echoes of the Void bridges the gap between dense NASA scientific repositories and middle-school/high-school STEM curricula. By turning passive reading into active experimentation, it empowers students to grasp real astrophysics concepts—such as the speed of light, planetary seismology, and heliospheric boundaries—while ensuring humanity's forgotten pioneers continue inspiring the next generation of explorers.
